10.1017/S0022112095003053.background: The paper models liquid impact through pressure impulse and incompressible boundary conditions.
10.1017/S0022112095003053.experiments: The abstract describes analytical impact examples; new experiments are unverified.
10.1017/S0022112095003053.locator: Crossref abstract: mathematical model and boundary conditions
10.1017/S0022112095003053.limits: A pressure impulse requires a specified geometry and pre-impact velocity field. Peak pressure additionally requires the temporal load profile.

10.1017/jfm.2016.463.background: Kelvin impulse organizes asymmetric bubble-collapse jets into distinct dynamical regimes.
10.1017/jfm.2016.463.experiments: Hundreds of high-speed recordings examined bubbles near solid and free boundaries and under variable gravity.
10.1017/jfm.2016.463.locator: Crossref abstract: jet drivers, high-speed visualizations, and three regimes
10.1017/jfm.2016.463.limits: These are re-entrant collapse jets. External PFC transfer jets need their own boundary conditions and calibration.

10.1017/jfm.2013.26.background: Pressure-pulse reflection at a capillary meniscus focuses an axisymmetric liquid jet.
10.1017/jfm.2013.26.experiments: Boundary-integral simulations were compared with experimental jet trajectories and velocities.
10.1017/jfm.2013.26.locator: Crossref abstract: pressure pulse, meniscus, and experimental comparison
10.1017/jfm.2013.26.limits: Meniscus geometry and capillary confinement are prescribed. The study does not establish the project's hydrogel outlet.

10.1017/jfm.2022.202.background: An extended Gilmore model connects laser-cavity thermodynamics with shock emission and energy partition.
10.1017/jfm.2022.202.experiments: Plasma photography, time-resolved shadowgraphs, and probe-beam scattering measured bubble growth and oscillations in water.
10.1017/jfm.2022.202.locator: Crossref abstract: measurements and extended Gilmore energy balance
10.1017/jfm.2022.202.limits: Optical breakdown in water differs from absorber-mediated PFC vaporization. Energy partition is case-specific.

10.1364/BOE.2.001432.background: Optically absorbing nanoparticles enable laser vaporization of weakly infrared-absorbing PFC droplets.
10.1364/BOE.2.001432.experiments: A 1064 nm laser activated PbS-loaded droplets, with optical, acoustic, and photoacoustic confirmation.
10.1364/BOE.2.001432.locator: Europe PMC DOI search: abstract methods
10.1364/BOE.2.001432.limits: The formulation uses micron-scale droplets and silica-coated PbS. The observed fluence cannot be transferred to an unspecified nanoscale inclusion.

10.1364/OL.39.002599.background: Gold-containing PFC nanoemulsions provide a photothermal route to cavitation-assisted clot disruption.
10.1364/OL.39.002599.experiments: The available project source identifies in vitro clot-disruption experiments; their detailed protocol remains unverified here.
10.1364/OL.39.002599.evidence: ?: metadata and preserved lesson citation; full methods unread
10.1364/OL.39.002599.limits: Clot disruption does not quantify transfer-jet launch, receiver loading, or printing yield.

10.1021/la701555n.background: Competing interface fracture determines rate-dependent pickup and release in transfer printing.
10.1021/la701555n.experiments: PDMS stamps peeled gold films from treated glass while video measured separation speed.
10.1021/la701555n.limits: The measured interfaces involve PDMS, gold, and glass. Their fracture parameters require remeasurement for the project stamp.

10.1073/pnas.2318739121.background: Water-vapor inflation in a hydrogel composite stamp switches adhesion for noncontact transfer.
10.1073/pnas.2318739121.experiments: Microscale silicon platelets were transferred onto diverse nonadhesive surfaces in planar and curved arrangements.
10.1073/pnas.2318739121.evidence: E: publisher-deposited and Europe PMC indexed abstracts
10.1073/pnas.2318739121.locator: Abstract: composite reservoir, water phase change, and transfer demonstrations
10.1073/pnas.2318739121.limits: The mechanism uses a sealed composite stamp and water vapor. External PFC jetting and bulk-gel channel formation remain separate mechanisms.

10.1017/S0022112000003347.background: Elastic-boundary recoil competes with bubble attraction to alter collapse and jet direction.
10.1017/S0022112000003347.experiments: High-speed imaging measured laser-generated bubbles, liquid jets, and boundary ejection near polyacrylamide gel.
10.1017/S0022112000003347.locator: Crossref abstract: elastic boundary, photography, and jet directions
10.1017/S0022112000003347.limits: The bubble lies adjacent to an elastic boundary. An embedded finite-mass PFC inclusion is a different geometry.

10.1017/jfm.2015.7.background: Finite-strain Kelvin-Voigt elasticity modifies spherical cavity oscillations in viscoelastic media.
10.1017/jfm.2015.7.experiments: The paper develops theoretical simulations; new experimental measurements remain unverified in the abstract.
10.1017/jfm.2015.7.locator: Crossref abstract: constitutive framework and elastic forces
10.1017/jfm.2015.7.limits: The medium is intact and the cavity is spherical. Rupture, heterogeneous damage, and outlets need additional models.

10.1017/S0022112094000480.background: A slender axisymmetric free-surface model predicts liquid-neck thinning and pinch-off.
10.1017/S0022112094000480.experiments: Model predictions were compared with existing jet-breakup and pendant-drop experiments.
10.1017/S0022112094000480.locator: Crossref abstract: one-dimensional equations and experimental comparisons
10.1017/S0022112094000480.limits: A slender jet must already exist. Its launch and receiver impact require separate descriptions.

10.1063/5.0045705.background: Near-wall bubble collapse can form a narrow high-speed liquid jet.
10.1063/5.0045705.experiments: Five-million-frame-per-second imaging with femtosecond illumination resolved laser-bubble needle jets near a solid surface.
10.1063/5.0045705.locator: Crossref abstract: seeded bubbles, surface proximity, and imaging
10.1063/5.0045705.limits: The narrow near-wall regime is geometry-specific. Reported speeds cannot be assigned to external transfer flow.

10.1103/PhysRevFluids.5.093604.background: Compressible near-wall bubble dynamics depend on bubble-to-boundary separation.
10.1103/PhysRevFluids.5.093604.experiments: The author preprint reports numerical distance sweeps; new experiments are unverified in its abstract.
10.1103/PhysRevFluids.5.093604.locator: arXiv abstract and related journal DOI
10.1103/PhysRevFluids.5.093604.limits: Numerical wall-jet benchmarks require matching geometry, compressibility, and resolution before project use.

10.1103/PhysRevFluids.2.093601.background: Bubble asymmetry changes collapse shock emission and energy distribution.
10.1103/PhysRevFluids.2.093601.experiments: The author preprint describes measurements of shock emission from nonspherical bubble collapses.
10.1103/PhysRevFluids.2.093601.limits: Shock emission and jet impact are distinct receiver-load observables.

10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.224501.background: Bubble interactions can alter shielding and collapse timing in ordered arrays.
10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.224501.experiments: The preserved lesson describes controlled multibubble surface-cavitation experiments; primary methods remain unread in this pass.
10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.224501.evidence: ?: preserved lesson summary and canonical metadata
10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.224501.limits: The experimental activation differs from laser/PFC arrays. Retain this as a benchmark lead until its primary methods are read.

10.1016/j.jmbbm.2024.106776.background: PFC phase change couples droplet properties with fast cavity inertia and slow gel-dependent evolution.
10.1016/j.jmbbm.2024.106776.experiments: Optical activation and imaging followed PFC droplets across inertial and quasi-static stages in gelatin, fibrin, and polyacrylamide.
10.1016/j.jmbbm.2024.106776.locator: Indexed abstract: three matrices, concentration, droplet size, and core composition
10.1016/j.jmbbm.2024.106776.limits: A bubble-radius record does not establish a directed external jet, receiver impact, or solid-payload transfer.

10.3390/nano13152238.background: PFC nanodroplet optical thresholds and reuse depend on shell composition and preconditioning.
10.3390/nano13152238.experiments: High-frame-rate ultrasound measured repeated optical vaporization while formulations and imaging parameters were varied.
10.3390/nano13152238.locator: Indexed abstract: thresholds, shells, preconditioning, and lifetimes
10.3390/nano13152238.limits: Population ultrasound onset differs from single-inclusion activation. Shell, temperature, and conditioning must match.

10.1021/acs.langmuir.4c05030.background: PFC droplet shells influence bubble growth and post-vaporization payload transport.
10.1021/acs.langmuir.4c05030.experiments: Optical microscopy and acoustic measurements compared lipid, protein, and polymer PFH droplets activated by ultrasound in fibrin.
10.1021/acs.langmuir.4c05030.locator: Indexed abstract: shell types, fibrin, microscopy, and ultrasound stimulation
10.1021/acs.langmuir.4c05030.limits: Optical characterization refers to imaging. The driving mechanism is acoustic droplet vaporization.

10.1021/acsami.5c11300.background: Phase-shift bubble dynamics and payload transport can evolve at different rates.
10.1021/acsami.5c11300.experiments: Brightfield, fluorescence, confocal imaging, and passive acoustic detection tracked ultrasound-activated PFC droplets in fibrin.
10.1021/acsami.5c11300.evidence: E: indexed abstract and figure captions
10.1021/acsami.5c11300.limits: Reported payload motion concerns acoustic activation in gel. It cannot calibrate laser-driven external transfer-jet speed.

10.1007/s10404-011-0787-4.background: Thin-film laser transfer permits external, re-entrant, and blister-driven jet mechanisms.
10.1007/s10404-011-0787-4.experiments: Time-resolved microscopy compared liquid ejection with metal and polymer absorbing layers.
10.1007/s10404-011-0787-4.locator: Abstract: gas cavities, external jets, re-entrant jets, and blister transition
10.1007/s10404-011-0787-4.limits: The absorber-layer and thin-film geometries require matching. None directly establishes an embedded-PFC outlet.

10.1017/jfm.2012.337.background: A deforming blister drives liquid-film ejection and a printable external jet.
10.1017/jfm.2012.337.experiments: Measured blister profiles drove simulations compared against jet shape, evolution, and released volume.
10.1017/jfm.2012.337.locator: Abstract: measured boundary motion and experimental comparison
10.1017/jfm.2012.337.limits: The driving boundary was measured. A pressure-only spherical model lacks that spatial launch input.

10.1007/s10404-013-1248-z.background: Absorber-mediated bubble generation changes jet stability and usable laser-printing conditions.
10.1007/s10404-013-1248-z.experiments: Time-resolved imaging compared release-layer-assisted and direct irradiation of silver ink, including deposited satellites.
10.1007/s10404-013-1248-z.locator: Abstract; issue date March 2014; online publication August 2013
10.1007/s10404-013-1248-z.limits: The canonical citation year is 2014; online publication occurred in 2013. Silver ink is a printing-mechanism analogue.

10.1063/5.0186998.background: Continuous-wave thermocavitation couples beam size, incubation time, heat transfer, and bubble energy.
10.1063/5.0186998.experiments: Water-filled microchannels were irradiated at 1950 nm and imaged while beam radius and laser power varied.
10.1063/5.0186998.locator: Sections 2 and 3: microchip, fiber positioning, imaging, and heat-transfer comparison
10.1063/5.0186998.limits: Continuous-wave water heating has different absorption and incubation scales from pulsed PFC activation.

10.1007/s11340-026-01332-z.background: Hydrogel network architecture governs material changes caused by repeated cavitation.
10.1007/s11340-026-01332-z.experiments: Five successive laser events were studied using high-speed imaging, confocal microscopy, and inverse rheometry in three gel networks.
10.1007/s11340-026-01332-z.locator: Experimental Methods; Laser Induced Cavitation; Assessing damage; Conclusions
10.1007/s11340-026-01332-z.limits: The fitted modulus is an effective damage proxy. Later cycles probe modified near-field material. Recovery requires separate waiting-time experiments.

10.1007/s42241-026-0020-2.background: Boundary stiffness and bubble separation determine elastic-wall jet and damage regimes.
10.1007/s42241-026-0020-2.experiments: High-speed photography compared laser-generated submillimeter bubbles near agarose boundaries of three concentrations.
10.1007/s42241-026-0020-2.locator: Abstract: high-speed photography, agarose boundaries, and regime classification
10.1007/s42241-026-0020-2.limits: The optimum separation belongs to an adjacent-boundary geometry. Transfer to embedded PFC inclusions remains an inference requiring experiments.

10.1088/1361-6633/adedb3.background: Optical breakdown links laser pulse conditions with plasma formation, bubble growth, and shock energy.
10.1088/1361-6633/adedb3.experiments: Plasma photography, probe-beam scattering, and absorption measurements examined tightly focused laser pulses in water.
10.1088/1361-6633/adedb3.limits: Journal publication is 2025; the accepted-manuscript revision is dated 2026. Breakdown energy fractions require matching to that water-plasma regime.

arxiv:2404.17457.background: A finite superheated droplet couples bubble motion with phase-change and heat-transfer balances.
arxiv:2404.17457.experiments: The abstract reports analytical-limit validation of a semi-analytical model; new experiments are unverified.
arxiv:2404.17457.locator: Abstract: motion, thermodynamics, convection-diffusion, and complete vaporization
arxiv:2404.17457.limits: The modeled system is water in oil. PFC properties and gel constitutive laws require substitution and validation.

10.3390/ijms23126636.background: Laser-generated cavities can create internal channels within cell-covered collagen microfibres.

10.3390/ijms23126636.locator: Pages 1-4: abstract, introduction, and channel-formation results
10.3390/ijms23126636.limits: This supports geometry-dependent channel formation in collagen. A reproducible PFC-powered outlet and external transfer remain unestablished.

10.1063/1.5060717.background: Paste rheology can permit repeated laser transfer from a replenishing donor spot.
10.1063/1.5060717.experiments: Industrial silver paste was printed with repeated pulses while solvent addition altered its rheology.
10.1063/1.5060717.locator: Crossref abstract: repeated same-spot printing and rheology modification
10.1063/1.5060717.limits: Healing occurs in a paste film. It does not establish recovery of a chemically crosslinked hydrogel.

10.1063/5.0123894.background: Bubble oscillations fragment droplets through multiple interface-jetting mechanisms.
10.1063/5.0123894.experiments: Single laser bubbles inside water microdroplets revealed crown jetting, oil-finger rupture, and induced jetting.
10.1063/5.0123894.limits: The geometry concerns water droplets and emulsification. Stable project transfer requires distinct breakup and deposition measurements.
